from.place: Proof paragraph 2: derived coefficient adjunction, via stable enhancement and final-index colimits; the normalized identity-cone criterion used in proving the final-vertex right-anodyne characterization. Auxiliary Equivalences into a vertex are the final objects of its join slice.

title: Equivalences into a vertex are the final objects of its join slice
statement: Use quasicategories, equivalence edges, right-pinched mapping spaces, Kan complexes and weak contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory, let $x,t$ be vertices, and let $f:x\to t$ be an edge. Regard $f$ as a vertex of the join slice $\mathcal C_{/t}$ defined in [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Then $f$ is an equivalence edge in $\mathcal C$ if and only if for every vertex $a\in\mathcal C_{/t}$ the right-pinched mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{/t}}(a,f)$ is a weakly contractible Kan complex. Equivalently, the equivalence arrows with target $t$ are precisely the final objects of this slice; this does not assume that $t$ itself is final in $\mathcal C$.
